- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”

Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 892 3466 1303, Password: 774734.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's

MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  OCTOBER 20, 2020

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Arata, Buresh, Carman, Corman,
  Seamans, Shinn, Stegura, Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Addleman, Bayer, Medawar, Silvano

  STUDENT MEMBERS PRESENT:  Scandaliato

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Robert Davis, Michael Baker International
  Dino Serafini, Michael Baker International
  Dan Wery, Michael Baker International
  Derek Wong, Michael Baker International
  Seth Contreras, Project Planner, Fehr & Peers
  John Muggridge, Principal, Fehr & Peers
  Peter Quintanilla, Fehr & Peers

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  SEPTEMBER 15, 2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
CORMAN to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 15, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

Written comment received by e-mail from Bruce Steckel, read to the committee stated the
following:
I know we are creating a long term plan, but the short term crisis we are in, needs to be
addressed. Or we should build in flexibility to the General Plan? For the duration of the COVID
restrictions on certain businesses as to capacity, can the City consider modifications to minimum
parking and use of common outside spaces to allow restaurants and retailers safe, open-air
use? Obvious health code and traffic and zoning issues need to be addressed. But if businesses
are forced to operate at less than break even capacity for another year or more, we will lose more
of our shops and eating establishments.
Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City has been approving Temporary Use Permits
primarily on private party parking lots. Staff conducted outreach going door-to-door to businesses.
The program is available and is a no fee permit. Director Wahba added that a permit was also
issued to a medical clinic on Deep Valley Drive to conduct COVID testing.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, OCTOBER 20, 2020
 CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that although this item was not agendized and cannot be discussed, she
asked that the GPAC members and those in attendance, to get the word out to businesses that
the City does have this program in place. Information can also be found on the website.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  COMMERCIAL DISTRICT DISCUSSION - MARKET AND PARKING STUDY
  HIGHLIGHTS, OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES, PRELIMINARY CONCEPTS.

John Bellas, Micheal Baker International (MBI), introduced the following members of the MBI
Team and members of Fehr & Peers joining the meeting tonight, as follows: Derek Wong and
Peter Serafini (MBI) worked on the market study for the commercial district; John Davis (MBI)
worked on the traffic study for the commercial district; Seth Contreras (Fehr & Peers) worked on
the transporation study; and, Peter Quintanilla, Urban Designer for MBI, worked on a design study
for the commercial district.

Mr. Bellas stated that the designs for the commercial district that will be presented are not
recommendations or alternatives, but rather possibilities based on what the market and parking
study, and other research revealed, as well as discussions at previous GPAC meetings.

Mr. Bellas stated that as part of their study - local, state, and even international case studies were
were considered and aspects of certain projects/localities were drawn from, to provide ideas for
the City.

Surabhi Barbhaya (MBI) stated that the discussion will be based on concepts and alternatives for
the commercial district and background on the market, parking, and mobility study.

Derek Wong (MBI) stated that he and Dino Serafini (MBI) worked on the market study for the
commercial district. The market study was divided into two work elements: 1) to review
opportunities for the non-residential or commercial aspects of the commercial distict; and 2) the
residential component of the market analysis. Mr. Wong provided an overview of their analysis,
which included four comparable shopping areas to the RHE Commercial Business District (RHE
CBD), which were identified as follows: The Point in El Segundo; Palisades Village in Pacific
Palisades; The Lab in Costa Mesa; and, Waterside in Marina del Rey. Each of these have a
leasing area of approximately 125,000 square feet.

A demographic comparison was presented, using a five-mile radius from the center of the five
shopping areas, and included: population, median age, median household incomes, and median
home value.

A slide was presented on a five-year forecast of the five shopping areas and their expected
consumer expenditures in major areas, such as: apparel, food, entertainment and recreation.
There are commonalities among the five shopping areas with the largest shopping areas being,
food for home, next is food going out and enetertainment, the least expenditure is apparel.

A slide showing the business types in the city’s shopping areas compared to those of shopping
areas outside of the city was presented. The business type with the highest percentage in the city
is, services, followed by retail and food. Other shopping areas have the highest percentages in
retail followed by food. In addition, the shopping centers in RHE tend to produce less sales per
square foot, with the exception of Town and Country, as compared to other comparable shopping
centers.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN asked if the businesses on the Pensinula are reflective of what
the consumer trends are, or are there just not businesses available for people to purchase. Mr.
Wong stated that the businesses are located closer to wealthier enclaves who have a particular
taste and as you go out the a few miles, the income levels drop.

COMMIITTEE MEMBER CARMAN asked if medical is included as part of servies. Mr. Wong
stated that in the business types, medical is included in services. In the expenditures slide,
medical is a separate category, which was not included.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked about the business types slide where food is not
broken down between food for home and food going out and the expenditure slide where they are

 broken down. Mr. Wong stated that in the expenditure slide, real estate data is provided and is
broken down. In the business type slide, they were combined for simplicity and anything non-retail
which is food related was included.

Director Wahba stated that Target was not included in these presentations.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS asked about a previous discussion on reconnecting Deep
Valley Drive from Penninusla Center to outside of the Promenade. CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that
in June, the GPAC had a visioning meeting and this was one of the things that committee
members would like to see.

Dino Serafini (MBI) presented the residential component of the market study. A series of pro
formas were prepared for the current residential projects and example projects that could be built
in the commercial district. Mr. Serafini stated that the pro forma calculates a residual land value
(RLV) for each project – critical assumptions and influential factors were explained.

A slide on residential opportunity sites was presented, using the following: Merrill Gardens
(existing), Deep Valley Road west of Roxcove Drive, Southwest corner Norris Center and Silver
Spur Road, Northwest corner Norris Center and Silver Spur Road.

Dan Wery (MBI) provided a presentation on examples of development types that are in or are
appropriate for RHE. All are 3-5 stories, include commercial on the ground floor and residential
above, and have tuck under parking.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA inquired about the need to do rezoning to allow for more units
per acre, in order to accommodate affordable housing requirements. Mr. Wery stated that the
intent of this presentation is to see what features the committee likes or dislikes and this will help
when discussing zoning and what features to consider or regulate. Currently zoning is 22 units
per acre.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS asked if mixed-use developments are still popular by
builders. Mr. Wery stated that it depends on the area, however, the country is over-retailed and it
is changing due to e-retail/e-commerce. A lot of mixed-use developments are struggling because
they are not self-supporting.

Ms. Stein, resident of 901 Deep Valley Drive, stated that one feature not included in the design is
green space. Ms. Stein also stated that in regards to on-street parking, visibility is already difficult
when exiting the building and cars on the street would make it more difficult. Mr. Wery stated that
when there is on-street parking around garages, there are setbacks in order to provide good
visibility and sightline to safely exit. In regards to green space, it is critical and this would be part
of having transitional space and streetscapes. Pedestrian crossing and truck traffic is also
something that will be addressed.

Ms. Katzer, resident and Board Member of 901 Deep Valley Drive, agreed with Ms. Stein
regarding green space and stated that it should be the responsibility of the builders and planners
to include park space to provide places to gather. She also expressed her concern with the impact
to traffic, parking, and pedestrians. Ms. Katzer stated that she has called the city regarding the
sign for the walkway at Deep Valley Drive and Roxcove, which is covered by a tree. She stated
that the corner needs a stop sign for the safety of pedestrians. Ms. Katzer asked why building
additional residences is being discussed as opposed to bringing in businesses.

Mr. Wery stated that the city has obligations to provide affordable housing and are looking for
where they can be built and the design parameters.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN asked why the focus is on residential use in the Silver Spur
area. There is a mandate to meet right now, but if this mandate were to be reversed, it would be
a shame to have all this density at the top of the hill.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE stated that some of the sites presented would be good for
needed modern office space. There are people who work locally and the buildings need to be
updated.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  3
 MINUTES, OCTOBER 20, 2020
 Mr. Wery provided a presentation on Mobility Trip Generation - Average Daily Trips (ADT)
comparing the main business types, including: restaurants, retail, office, and apartments with
100,000 sq. ft. of space. The most intense trip generation is restaurants at 11,000 ADT, followed
by retail at 3,750 ADT, office at 1,000 ADT, and 100 apartments at 750 ADT. In addition, Mr. Wery
presented a a slide showing the impact during peak hours and pointed out that having a mix of
uses is good for traffic.

Peter Quintanilla (Fehr & Peers) provided a presentation of conceptual designs for the commercial
district. Connections within five minutes to shopping centers were incorporated as well as designs
breaking up the Promenade Shopping Center with various uses. Mr. Quintanilla also provided
ideas for parking in various areas throughout the commercial district.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that this presumes significant demolition of existing
floor area that is under lengthy lease terms. Mr. Wery stated that this a long term concept and
want to make sure that the ideas being proposed are viable options. In terms of the mall, over a
third of the space is vacant, which can be repurposed or replaced.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that putting multi-family at the corners of Silver
Spur and Norris Drive has a lot of merit.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS appreciated Mr. Quintanilla’s ideas and asked how a project
like this could be financed and how a community space could be incorporated. Mr. Wery stated
that most of these ideas would be implemented by the property owners and they would need to
determine if this if in their financial best interest. Regarding the community spaces, Mr. Quintanilla
showed various ideas for large or small spaces that can be used for this purpose.

CHAIR SCHMITZ commended Mr. Quintanilla on presenting these ideas to the committee and
providing what can be, in the future.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA thanked Mr. Quintanilla and asked about how much vehicle,
bike, and pedestrian traffic is being envisioned at the spine that was shown at Deep Valley Drive.
Mr. Quintanilla stated that there is an opportunity to create something new; a generous sidewalk,
protected bike lane, and parallel parking would be great.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BURESH stated that these were interesting ideas, but does not foresee
developers giving up land to put in streets. Committee Member Buresh suggested finding a way
to make the Promenade work since a lot of money was spent renovating it. In addition, the
development on Deep Valley Drive is built to the sidewalk and it is uncomfortable to walk past
there and setbacks are important especially if considering walkability.

STUDENT MEMBER SCANDALIATO asked about the buildings on Bart Earle Way and if the
suggestion is to move the buildings next to the Red Onion to Silver Spur. Mr. Quintanilla stated
that the space where the existing buildings are, would be used for parking space.
In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Wery stated that Silver
Spur has the capacity to handle traffic and service the buildings if they were to come to Bart Earle
Way. That would be providing property to be used for private development. Mr. Bellas added that
that the parking lots behind the buildings are already providing a drive aisle.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE suggested a one-way street with a bike lane on Deep Valley
Drive coming up from Silver Spur Road. This would slow down traffic and the people living on the
street would have better access getting through one lane of traffic. Mr. Quintanilla stated that this
could be looked into.

6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF/COMMITTEE ITEMS

Ms. Barbhaya stated that next step in the Land Use Element would be to look at the city overall,
look at alternatives, and look at policy discussion items. Some of the items discussed will be used
for the policies that will be developed going forward. As part of the General Plan, an area plan
needs to be developed and the intent of this meeting was to create an area plan for the
commercial distict.

Mr. Bellas stated that at the next meeting, the results of the parking study will be presented and
then move on to the land uses in the rest of the city.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  4
 MINUTES, OCTOBER 20, 2020
 CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that at the next meeting, a few minutes will be dedicated to give the
committee an opportunity to comment on items from this meeting. Mr. Bellas stated that slides
from the presentation will be provided to the committee.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee and adjourned the meeting at 8:12 p.m.

The next General Plan Advisory Committee meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 17, 2020
at 6:00 p.m. via Video Teleconference.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,

______________________________  ______________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Velveth, Schmitz, Chair
